release_scope: v0.1.0 — Protected File Mutation Profile v1

status_vocabulary.SPECIFIED: Stated in the paper or SPEC.md; not implemented or not tested here.
status_vocabulary.IMPLEMENTED: Code exists; no dedicated test evidence yet.
status_vocabulary.LOCALLY_TESTED: Implemented and exercised by the committed, deterministic test/attack corpus on the author's side. Not independently reproduced.
status_vocabulary.REPRODUCED: Independently reproduced by someone other than the author.
status_vocabulary.INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED: Reviewed by an independent party with a published report.
status_vocabulary.PRODUCTION_VALIDATED: Validated in a production deployment with evidence.
status_vocabulary.OPEN: Not established; an outside engineer could design a test or proof for it.
status_vocabulary.RESIDUAL: Outside the theorem's boundary by declaration (paper section 10.15).
status_vocabulary.NOT_APPLICABLE: Does not apply to this release.

epistemic_labels.S: Security or invariant claim dependent on trusted-system conditions

claims.text: For the declared attack corpus, no unauthorized mutation of the two protected files occurred when requests went through the reference monitor.
assumptions: C1 (partial: declared effect surface only, not established)
limitations: Finite corpus; zero observed failures do not prove zero real-world risk
No complete-mediation proof
No independent audit

claims.text: A capability is bound to one principal, one effect and one resource; substitution of any of the three is blocked, and edits to a signed capability are detected.
limitations: HMAC (symmetric): compromise of the monitor implies capability forgery
Principal attribution is by declared id; no authentication of the requesting process

claims.text: Expired, not-yet-valid and revoked capabilities (by id or by epoch) are rejected.
limitations: Time comes from the host clock; clock tampering is out of scope
Revocation store is in-memory in v0.1

claims.text: A single-use capability cannot be spent twice, including under concurrent attempts within one process.
limitations: Atomicity comes from one in-process lock; multi-process or distributed atomicity is not demonstrated
State/version binding independently blocks replays, so the single-use check is redundant for version-bound capabilities (reported by the ablation)

claims.text: Resource state is revalidated at execution time; a capability issued for a superseded version is rejected.
limitations: Revalidation and commit are atomic only with respect to other mediated requests
Non-mediated writers are detected afterwards (CLM-009), not excluded

claims.text: Unresolvable safety state (policy, revocation, resource metadata, evidence witness) is treated as UNKNOWN and mapped to BLOCK.
limitations: Failures are injected by test doubles, not by real infrastructure faults
If the evidence witness fails after commit, the effect has already happened; the gap is reported, not prevented

claims.text: Capabilities are bound to the active policy hash, a deny-by-default policy is evaluated per request, and candidate policies are statically checked at admission against the Safety Profile.
limitations: Restricted exact-match language; executable admission check only
No proof object and no machine-checked refinement checker (paper condition C4/PAV remains open)

claims.text: Every mediated request produces a structured, hash-chained evidence record from which the request, the checks passed or failed, and the outcome can be reconstructed.
limitations: Local log only; no external witness
Hash chain detects naive tampering; it does not establish legal non-repudiation
Evidence completeness across alternate paths is not established

claims.text: A change to a protected file made through a non-mediated channel is detected on the next mediated request and that request is blocked.
limitations: Detection after the fact, not prevention
An attacker who also rewrites the version sidecar consistently is not detected by this mechanism

claims.text: Complete mediation of the protected effect surface (condition C1).
limitations: v0.1 runs monitor and mediated code in one process and uid; direct writes are possible (bypass probe)
Roadmap v0.2: OS-level privilege separation and alternate-path tests

claims.text: Conformance of the monitor to verified semantics (kernel conformance, C3) and integrity of the trusted core (C2).
limitations: No formal verification or kernel-level assurance
Trusted core is small (governor/*.py) but unproven

claims.text: Machine-checked typed refinement from the deployed policy to the admitted safety constitution (C4).
limitations: Roadmap v0.3

claims.text: Capability delegation with attenuation (child scope, budget and expiry bounded by the parent).
limitations: Not implemented; capabilities naming a parent are rejected (tested), nothing more
Roadmap v0.4

claims.text: Independent security review, external red-team validation and held-out adaptive evaluation.
limitations: None performed; invitations to falsify are in SECURITY.md and AUDIT.md

claims.text: Conditional Behavioral Safety Theorem: under C1-C8 every executed protected effect satisfies the admitted safety predicate.
limitations: Conditional on all eight conditions; this prototype demonstrates only a subset (see CLM-001..CLM-009 and CLM-010..CLM-012)

claims.text: L1 (public-ground component) and NRD (no unjustified normative difference), plus the constitutional-reflexivity constraint CR/CAR, as derived in the paper's practice-based ethics.
assumptions: Paper premises P1 and following; classical first-order logic
limitations: Derivations are not machine-checked (paper section 10.13)
Substantive standards B4-B8 are declared (A), not derived
This repository does not implement or test the philosophical layer

claims.text: Semantic assurance (G-Osem): calibrated probabilistic bounds on neural state extraction.
limitations: The v0.1 monitor is purely mechanical and makes no semantic judgments

claims.text: Covert channels, unmediated physical effects, compromised root of trust and operator-controlled disabling are outside the guarantee.
limitations: These are the boundary of the theorem, not defects of terminology
